subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WebSocket origin gate reusing checkBrowserOrigin

question: Should the existing Control UI origin policy become a pre-upgrade admission rule for every Origin-bearing Gateway WebSocket client, or only for the browser/control-UI client class it currently governs?
rationale: `verifyClient` executes before a client is classified, so choosing its scope changes the compatibility and security contract for all Origin-bearing upgrade clients.

options.title: Preserve the current client-aware scope
options.body: Refactor the pre-upgrade gate so it runs only when the request can be safely identified as the browser/control-UI admission path, then prove non-UI and proxy cases remain accepted.

options.title: Adopt a global Origin-bearing-client policy
options.body: Approve the broader admission contract explicitly, document affected integrations and proxy behavior, and add regression coverage for the intended rejects.

recommendation.title: Preserve the current client-aware scope
recommendation.body: Refactor the pre-upgrade gate so it runs only when the request can be safely identified as the browser/control-UI admission path, then prove non-UI and proxy cases remain accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership could not be established from the supplied context; a gateway/security owner should make this contract decision.
